item.title: FIFA scraps its World Cup investment plan after backlash
item.description: FIFA is shelving a controversial plan that would have allowed for billions of dollars in private commercial investment in the World Cup after the proposal was met with fierce opposition from its member nations.

item.title: Body of missing girl found in New Jersey river after 2-day search, officials say
item.description: The body of a missing girl has been found in the Passaic River in New Jersey after a two-day search, officials said.

item.title: Spain sends over 48,000 migrants back to Morocco from Ceuta; dozens dead
item.description: Spain's Ministry of the Interior said about 50,000 people entered the Spanish enclave since Thursday morning, with an estimated 48,300 back in Morocco by 6 p.m. Friday.

item.title: A timeline of Nancy Guthrie's disappearance as search stretches on
item.description: Savannah Guthrie's mom, Nancy Guthrie, was reported missing Feb. 1.

item.title: 60,000 migrants poured into Spain from Morocco, Ceuta's president says, but many already left
item.description: According to the president of Ceuta, 60,000 migrants have flooded the small Spanish territory from Morocco since Thursday. Most voluntarily left the territory amid shortages of food, water and shelter, but thousands remained. Spain's prime minister called it an attack. Aiden Stretch reports from Ceuta, Spain.

item.title: After a stranger gifts a boy with autism a piano, he dazzles the world: "He's Mozart level"
item.description: Back in 2023, a stranger gifted a boy with autism a piano after seeing his story on the local news. Now, the stranger is more like family, and the boy is dazzling the world with his music. Steve Hartman goes "On the Road" revisiting Jude's story.

item.title: U.S. probing if Iran was behind cyberattack on water systems in 7 states
item.description: Malicious cyber activity affected technology at water systems in at least seven states this week, including Minnesota, leading authorities to dig into whether Iranian actors are behind the attack, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Oil giants see profits surge as Iran war drives energy prices higher
item.description: America's biggest oil companies are reporting massive profits as the Iran war continues to disrupt global energy supplies. CBS News business contributor Javier David joins with analysis.

item.title: DOJ to dismiss Reflecting Pool vandalism charges, citing "botched installation"
item.description: Federal prosecutors moved to dismiss an indictment charging U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn with ripping the bottom of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, saying the damage was caused by "botched installation and not vandalism."

item.title: DOJ drops case against former Olympian accused of damaging Reflecting Pool
item.description: The U.S. government dismissed the felony indictment against David Hearn, the former Olympian accused of damaging the Reflecting Pool of the National Mall.

item.title: Trump blames Minnesota cyber attacks on its governor, not Iran
item.description: President Trump took his Cabinet meeting on the road to Camp David on Friday, where he downplayed cyberattacks on Minnesota water systems that U.S. officials suspect were linked to Iran. Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Extended heat wave risks lives, increases fire danger and drought
item.description: The heat that baked the South earlier this week moved west under a so-called heat dome. More than 70 million people are under alert for life-threatening heat conditions. Jason Allen reports from Oklahoma City.

item.title: U.S. preparing new Iran strikes as Trump says, "We've done an amazing job"
item.description: There was no sign of the conflict ending as Iran claimed to have struck two ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie ransom notes are released, including message saying she died
item.description: One of the notes threatened to kill Nancy Guthrie if a multimillion-dollar ransom wasn't paid in a week. The second, a few days later, says, "She is buried in nature now."

item.title: U.S., Israel preparing to bombard energy-related targets in Iran, sources say
item.description: The U.S. and Israel plan to hit Iran's energy infrastructure as soon as this weekend, although no final decision has been made, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Both ransom notes in Nancy Guthrie case released by police
item.description: For the first time, the Pima County Sheriff's Office released a pair of emails allegedly sent by Nancy Guthrie's kidnapper, who said she had died shortly after she had been abducted. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: New show inspired by the 1990s classic "Clueless" to begin shooting next year
item.description: A new series based on the beloved 1995 film "Clueless" is coming to Paramount+, with original star Alicia Silverstone returning. SiriusXM radio host Lamar Dawson joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: U.S, Israel planning harshest attacks yet on energy-related sites in Iran, sources say
item.description: The U.S. and Israel are planning the most significant strikes yet on Iran's energy infrastructure, multiple sources say. President Trump has threatened this multiple times in recent months. Margaret Brennan has more details.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie ransom notes released by Pima County Sheriff's Department
item.description: Possible ransom notes released by the Pima County Sheriff's Department in the hopes of identifying Nancy Guthrie's kidnapper or kidnappers include specific details about Guthrie's white Apple Watch and allege that she died unexpectedly of a medical condition and "is buried in nature." CBS News' Anna Schecter breaks it down.

item.title: Pilot of F-35 military jet that crashed in San Diego in stable condition after ejecting
item.description: The pilot of the F-35 that crashed at Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in San Diego, California, on Friday is in stable condition with non-life-threatening injuries. CBS News' Carter Evans has the details.

item.title: Trump says Hamas agreed to next phase of Gaza peace deal, including disarmament
item.description: President Trump announced that Hamas agreed to a ceasefire negotiated by the Board of Peace, which would include total disarmament. CBS News' national security contributor Samantha Vinograd breaks down what we know so far.

item.title: "Sunday Morning" show times
item.description: Stations carrying CBS' Emmy Award-winning morning program.

item.title: U.S. and Israel preparing to bomb Iran's energy infrastructure, sources say
item.description: Sources told CBS News on Friday that the U.S. and Israel are planning to bomb energy-related infrastructure in Iran. The unconfirmed strikes could take place throughout the weekend. CBS News' James LaPorta and Olivia Rinaldi have more.

item.title: Doctors testify in Lindsay Clancy trial, jury views home where 3 kids were killed
item.description: Day 4 of the Lindsay Clancy murder trial started with a jury visit to her former Duxbury, Massachusetts home where her three kids were killed.

item.title: Nearly 1 in 4 Americans want CEOs to "stop being greedy," survey finds
item.description: New poll explores what people wish corporate leaders understood about economic life in the U.S. today.

item.title: 75% say their income isn't keeping up with inflation, CBS News poll finds
item.description: New CBS News polling shows many Americans don't think President Trump is doing enough to bring down prices. Political strategists Rina Shah and Amirah Sequeira join with analysis.

item.title: Epstein survivor Dani Bensky calls Todd Blanche "walking perjury"
item.description: Survivors of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's abuse were on Capitol Hill this week lobbying senators to reject Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general. One survivor, Dani Bensky, joins "The Takeout" to discuss her concerns about Blanche.

item.title: 7/31: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: President Trump holds Cabinet meeting at Camp David; 7 states report cyberattack on water systems.

item.title: OCTROT heated blankets and throws recalled after fires and injuries
item.description: Chinese-made electric bedding poses "risk of serious injury or death," according to U.S. product safety regulators.

item.title: Inside a California data center as communities raise concerns about energy costs
item.description: California lawmakers are considering several proposals affecting data centers, including bills intended to shield utility customers from increased electricity costs.
